facts.text: I am trying to decide between building a new gaming PC or buying a new graphics card for my current one.
I want to play Cyberpunk 2077 at its highest settings.
My current CPU is an Intel Core i5-11600K.
My motherboard is an ASRock B460M Steel Legend Micro ATX.
I have 16 GB of DDR4 RAM at 3200MHz.
My current graphics card is an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060.
My budget for the upgrade or new build is around $1,500.
I watched a lot of videos on IGN and GameSpot to catch up on the latest gaming news and updates.
I completed The Last of Us Part II on my PlayStation 5 after playing it for 10 hours last weekend.
I played The Last of Us Part II on a PlayStation 5.
I was invested in the story and characters, especially Ellie and Abby.
One of my favorite moments was when I finally defeated a boss that had been giving me trouble for weeks.
I think Abby's character arc was really well done.
I appreciated how The Last of Us Part II humanized Abby and showed her vulnerabilities.
I did not expect to feel sympathetic towards Abby at first.
As the story progressed, I started to understand Abby's motivations and feel for her.
I loved how Abby's relationship with Lev was well-written.
I have been following updates and rumors about The Elder Scrolls 6.
I am excited to see what Bethesda comes up with for The Elder Scrolls 6.
I have always loved the Elder Scrolls series.
Skyrim is one of my favorite games of all time.
I am hoping The Elder Scrolls 6 will have a similar sense of scope and exploration.
I am hoping The Elder Scrolls 6 will have more advanced gameplay mechanics.
I am hoping The Elder Scrolls 6 will have a more immersive story.
I am curious to see how The Elder Scrolls 6 will incorporate the province of Hammerfell and the Redguard culture.
I think Hammerfell and Redguard culture are a great opportunity to explore a new region and learn more about Elder Scrolls lore.
I am curious about rumors of a potential multiplayer component for The Elder Scrolls 6.
I would be interested in playing The Elder Scrolls 6 with friends.
I am also considering whether The Elder Scrolls 6 should remain a single-player experience.
